answer.sourceLine: Ginsburg said this at the Radcliffe Day luncheon at Harvard on 29 May 2015, answering a question about the advice she would give young women today. The wording is confirmed verbatim by the host institution and contemporaneous news coverage — a rare case of a “famous name” quote that is genuinely theirs.

author.name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
author.heading: About Ruth Bader Ginsburg
author.metaLine: 1933–2020 · U.S. Supreme Court Justice & pioneering women’s-rights litigator
author.bio: Ruth Bader Ginsburg argued a landmark series of sex-discrimination cases before the Supreme Court in the 1970s as head of the ACLU Women’s Rights Project, then served as an Associate Justice of that same Court from 1993 until her death in 2020. Known for her precise, incremental advocacy and pointed dissents, she became a cultural icon in her final decade. This quote — her advice to young women — distills her method: press hard for your cause, but in a way that wins allies rather than repels them.
